title: Kestrel Token Vault (KTV) Release 2 — High-Level Design

expected_findings.title: No real-time alerting on break-glass account use in the CDE
expected_findings.description: The break-glass IAM user bypasses the PAM approval and FIDO2 controls, yet its use is only reviewed in the monthly access review and is not among the SIEM alerts triaged by the SOC (which cover PAM grants, HSM administration and configuration changes). Misuse of the most privileged path into the cardholder data environment could therefore go unnoticed for weeks. Recommend a real-time SIEM/CloudTrail alert on any sign-in or activity by the break-glass user, with mandatory post-use review.
evidence: A break-glass IAM user exists for use when the IdP or PAM tool is unavailable; its password and hardware MFA token are split between two custodians and kept in the corporate safe.
Break-glass sessions are reviewed during the monthly access review.

expected_findings.title: Long-lived, manually renewed mTLS workload certificates
expected_findings.description: Client certificates that authorise callers (including the detokenize identities) are valid for three years and renewed by hand. A stolen private key stays useful for a long time unless the compromise is detected and the certificate revoked, and manual renewal risks outages and inconsistent handling. Recommend short-lived certificates (for example 30-90 days) issued and rotated automatically, e.g. via cert-manager with AWS Private CA.
evidence: Workload client certificates are issued by the Payments private CA with a three-year validity and are renewed manually by the platform team ahead of expiry.

must_not_flag.title: Cardholder PANs stored unencrypted in the vault database
must_not_flag.why_not: Section 6 states the vault holds PANs and expiry dates only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext under HSM-resident keys that never leave the HSM in plaintext; the Aurora storage is additionally KMS-encrypted.
evidence: Card numbers are stored in the vault database alongside the token, the card expiry date and the merchant identifier.

The vault stores PANs and expiry dates only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext under data-encryption keys generated and held in the CloudHSM cluster; encryption and decryption happen inside the HSM and keys never leave it in plaintext.

must_not_flag.title: Detokenization API exposes full PANs to callers
must_not_flag.why_not: Section 5.1 restricts detokenize to two named mTLS client identities and rejects all others with 403 before the vault is queried; section 7 alerts on detokenize volume anomalies and any rejected caller.
evidence: The Detokenization API accepts a token and returns the full PAN in the response body.
The detokenize operation is restricted to the settlement-batch and chargeback-svc identities; requests presenting any other certificate are rejected with HTTP 403 before the vault is queried.

must_not_flag.title: Tokens leak PAN digits / tokens are reversible
must_not_flag.why_not: Section 6 states the non-retained token digits come from the HSM RNG with no mathematical relationship to the PAN, and last-four display is within PCI DSS masking rules.
evidence: Tokens are 16 digits long, deliberately fail the Luhn check, and keep the last four digits of the original card number so that receipts and customer-care screens can display them.
Token digits other than the last four are generated by the HSM random number generator and have no mathematical relationship to the PAN, so a token cannot be converted back without a vault lookup.

must_not_flag.title: Cardholder data leaking to the SIEM outside the CDE
must_not_flag.why_not: Section 7 states PANs, expiry dates and CVV are never logged and the logging sidecar drops any Luhn-valid 13-19 digit sequence before events leave the pod; transport is TLS.
evidence: Application and audit logs from the CDE are forwarded to the corporate SIEM, which is hosted in the shared security tooling account outside the cardholder data environment.
PANs, expiry dates and CVV values are never written to logs; the Fluent Bit sidecar also drops any 13–19 digit sequence that passes a Luhn check before events leave the pod.

must_not_flag.title: Vault backups copied outside the CDE / backups not protected
must_not_flag.why_not: Section 9 states the backup account is in PCI DSS scope with no standing human access, snapshots hold only HSM-encrypted PANs plus a backup-account KMS key, and the vault uses Vault Lock in compliance mode (immutable).
evidence: A nightly AWS Backup job copies vault database snapshots to a separate AWS account, ktv-backup, for long-term retention.
Snapshots contain only HSM-encrypted PANs and are additionally encrypted with a KMS key owned by the backup account, which is within the PCI DSS assessment scope and has no standing human access.
The ktv-backup account stores the nightly snapshots in an AWS Backup vault with Vault Lock in compliance mode and one-year retention.

must_not_flag.title: Encryption keys duplicated to the DR region / key exposure during replication
must_not_flag.why_not: Section 6 states key material moves between HSM clusters only as encrypted CloudHSM backups and is never exported in plaintext outside an HSM boundary; a DR key copy is required for failover.
evidence: The CloudHSM cluster in eu-west-1 holds copies of all production data-encryption keys so that detokenization can continue after a regional failover.
Key material is copied between HSM clusters only as encrypted CloudHSM backups; keys are never exported in plaintext outside an HSM boundary.
